recipes.name: Sunday Best Fruit Salad
ingredients_raw: 1 (20 ounce) can pineapple chunks, juice reserved

steps.text: In a small bowl, toss the chopped apples in reserved pineapple juice. Allow to sit for 5 to 10 minutes.
In a large salad bowl, combine the peach pie filling and pineapple chunks.
Remove apples from pineapple juice and add to pie filling and pineapple mixture. Add chopped bananas to reserved pineapple juice and let sit for 5 to 10 minutes.
Peel and slice kiwi and 1/2 of strawberries. Chop the other 1/2 of strawberries and set aside.
Remove bananas from pineapple juice and add to pie filling mixture. Add chopped strawberries; toss together.
Arrange kiwi slices around the edge of the serving bowl and alternate with strawberry slices. Chill and serve.

raw_recipe.headline: Sunday Best Fruit Salad
raw_recipe.description: Several steps build to the final salad crescendo. Chopped apples and bananas marinate in pineapple juice, and kiwi and strawberries are sliced. Then everything is mixed into peach pie filling and spooned into a beautiful serving bowl.

video.description: Delicious fruits are soaked in pineapple juice and coated in sweet peach pie filling! Use bananas, apples, strawberries, and kiwi!
video.name: How to Make Sunday Fruit Salad

review.reviewBody:
Very good! I added grapes and mandarin oranges to the mix. I doubled the recipe except for the peach pie filling: I left that at one can, as I didn't want it to be overly sweet or slimy. It covered perfectly! Soaking the apples and bananas in the pineapple juice is pure genius! None of the fruit turned brown. A couple of notes: Make sure you drain all your fruit well because it will get sloppy quick. And the recipe states to arrange the kiwi on top for a reason. I got lazy & simply threw them in & after a couple of turns with the spoon, they promptly fell apart. 
Still very tasty though! Thanks for the recipe!

This is the best fruit salad ever. I used a mix of bananas,apples,strawberries,blueberries and green grapes I cut into two pieces. I use Fruit Fresh in my James so I put a teaspoon in a little water,mixed it and swirled the apples and bananas in it so they won't turn dark. I got them out and patted them dry so I didn't add water to the mix. My husband can't get enough of it and I have sent it to several friends. The fruit possibilities are beyond measure.

I add all of the strawberries and kiwi (diced/chopped) directly to this instead of laying them on top. Honestly though, it works well if you leave everything in large chunks and dump it all into a blender at once. You just have to be careful to only blend JUST enough to mix and dice your fruit or it will all turn to juice. I serve this as fruit salsa paired with homemade cinnamon tortilla chips or store bought cinnamon pita chips. 

One note... I add a lot of freshly squeezed lime juice to my pineapple juice and separate it evenly into two bowls, one for apples and one for bananas, for two reasons: 1. The best cook I know told me that lime is the best preventer of browning 2. I'm out on chopping stuff at different times during prep so I just do everything at the beginning and soak the apples and bananas simultaneously

This was good and very simple. For the most part I followed the recipe. In the begining I put the bananas and apples in a bowl and then poured the pineapple juice over the top and sprinkled some lemon juice on top as well. I let that sit for about 10 minutes. Then I dumped the peaches in my trifle bowl and mixed in the pineapple pieces. Next I put the apples and bananas in WITHOUT the pineapple juice. I mixed that together gently so the bananas didn't get mushy. Then I put 1/2 the strawberries on the top, added seedless red grapes and mixed it around a little more. Last I put the kiwi on top and stuck a few pieces down the sides and sprinkled the remaining strawberries on top as well. It was really good but next time I think I might use fresh pineapple & peaches and not worry about the gel from the peach pie mixture. The canned peaches were not very sweet while the gel was so I felt like if I had used fresh peaches and fresh pineapple it would have made up for the sweetness. However, I would still get a can of pineapple just to use the juice because that kept the bananas and apples didn't turn brown at all even with the salad sitting out all afternoon!

Use any fresh fruits and the pineapple really does keep the apple from "browning". I didn't have peach pie fill so I added a can of peaches (reserving the juice). Put the juice into small saucepan, add 1 Tbsp. corn starch and mix well. Heat until thickened. Cool, add to fuit. Delicious!

Yum! I was pleasantly surprised. I was skeptical of the pie filling. Make choices in the fruit, but the pie filling is what makes this recipe unique. I also used green grapes, black cherries and fresh pineapple. I mixed the fruit with the pie filling and put it in a huge container. I saved the canned pineapple for a stir-fry the next night, but used the juice for soaking as directed. With the huge amount of fruit, one can of pie filling was perfect. By the time I took it to the party, the fruit had released a little juice and it thinned the pie filling a bit. Everybody loved it and the addition of apples gave it a bit of crunch. Don't worry about making it ahead of time and adding the fragile fruit right before serving.
I made this recipe for my daughters wedding party,it was a big hit,everybody loved it.I used grapes and mandarin oranges also,and made it the day before it was still a beautiful salad

Got a similar recipe from Southern Living magazine decades ago and it has been a favorite with our family friends. It is much improved by adding fresh blueberries, grapes, orange slices - any of the firmer fruits. Not only are the additional fruits tasty but they dilute the pie filling which otherwise can be too sweet.

I have to confess, I was in a hurry so I didn't really follow the directions perfectly. I bought several quarts of pre-cut fruit including assorted berries, cantelope, etc. I forgot the bananas and apples but I did remember the peach pie filling. In searching for fruit salad recipes, I came upon a version elsewhere where the cook added Limoncello, a lemonie Italian liquor. It was amazing.

I rate this recipe 5-stars. I carried this to our Sunday School breakfast for 15 and it was a "hit". Many questions of the secret ingredient. I only made recipe for 8 and added 2-cups each of fresh blueberries and sliced red grapes. Refrigerated all ingredients overnight except peach pie filling. Added this Sunday morning. Absolutely beautiful. After reading comments I did add the vanilla flavoring and cinnamon to pie filling. Recipe for 8 with my additions was ample with some leftover. I will use this recipe whenever a fruit salad is needed!!!

This salad was a huge hit at my daughters graduation party! I added one small can of mandarin oranges and substituted apricot pie filling for the peach pie filling, as I couldn't find the peach flavor in my local stores. The apricot was awesome and added a touch of tangy-ness to it. It was also a smaller can, which I was concerned about, but it worked out perfectly for the sweetness I wanted. I made the salad "as is" and it was a great size for the party of 12-15. Will definitely make it again.
it was good!!!!!

I made this for Easter dinner. Everyone said it was good, but no one raved. I added grapes and blueberries, so I had more fruit than the recipe calls for, but I still thought the goo from the pie filling made the fruit seem slimy. The taste is good, however. I'm not sure I would make it again, but if I did I wouldn't add all the goo from the pie filling. I cut the peaches into smaller pieces to make them more the size of the other pieces of fruit.
Very good
SO DELICIOUS!
This is super good for the summer healthy recipe, and I wanted to put some whipped cream on it.

The decorative fruit on the top is the best part of this recipe. If you like fresh fruit salads, this will not be a winning recipe for you. The peach pie filling makes the consistency gooey, although the salad tastes fine. I plan to use the decorative presentation over fresh fruit compilation. Thanks for the suggestion!

Made the Sunday Best Fruit Salad for Thanksgiving. I added a pack of all the berries the grocery store had left out the bananas as I have an allergic child and it was gobbled up! The apples in the pineapple juice worked wonders...apples did not change color! I am making it again for Christmas
Great recipe. Made it for family Easter dinner and it got rave reviews. As another
Great salad for holidays; sweetness is perfect. Pie filling doesn't make it gooey
